podcast.body: The opening song and lead-off track from "Kid A." It was the first song Tom Yorke wrote on a brand new grand piano, despite the instrument not being heard in the final track. When fans first heard it, it clearly signaled the band's new, different direction. It was written in the same week as "Pyramid Song." "It was the first song that Tom wrote on a brand new grand piano."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This track is from Radiohead's 2000 album "Kid A," an album whose artwork is reputed to harbor intriguing secrets. "Radiohead and everything in its right place from Kid A, the artwork of which offers up some interesting secrets."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This was the first single released from the album *Kid A*, surprising pretty much everyone with its atmospheric, cinematic, and sonic journey qualities, characteristic of post-rock. "And when the first single was released, it surprised pretty much everyone. Here's everything in its right place."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
